claim.quote: An exclusion limit at the 95% confidence level on the mass of the gluino is set at 2.30 TeV for a simplified model containing only a gluino and the lightest neutralino, assuming the latter is massless.

name: Exclusion limits on squarks and gluinos from the full Run 2 dataset

significance.note: An exclusion limit; the analysis reports no significant excess over the Standard Model background.

summary.plain: ATLAS searched its full second run of LHC data for supersymmetric partner particles called squarks and gluinos, found no sign of them, and used that to rule out gluinos lighter than about 2.3 trillion electronvolts under a simple model.
summary.technical: Search for squarks and gluinos in jets + missing transverse momentum final states using the full Run 2 dataset (139 fb^-1 at 13 TeV): no significant excess observed; 95% CL exclusion of gluino masses up to 2.30 TeV in a simplified model with a massless lightest neutralino, extending earlier limits.

title: Search for squarks and gluinos in final states with jets and missing transverse momentum using 139 fb^-1 of sqrt(s)=13 TeV pp collision data with the ATLAS detector
why_it_matters: This is ATLAS's most stringent Run 2 exclusion of a leading class of supersymmetric partner particles, a landmark limit that shapes the remaining parameter space searched at the HL-LHC.
